City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
October 15, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on October 15, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on October 10, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley
INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission Viejo v. the State of California, Case No. 34 2012 8000 1203.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City prevailed in its litigation against the State and the County. The lawsuit was related to the $2.7 miscalculation by the County Auditor-Controller (as supported by the State Department of Finance.) Mr. Curley noted that this is a big win for the City and the money will now remain in the City’s coffers.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Presentation by Building Official Jay Elbettar Regarding "Homeowner’s Night" at City Hall, and the October 27, 2012 "Home Improvement Permitting Day" at Home Depot
The City Council received the presentation from Building Official Jay Elbettar.
P2.
Recognize City Volunteers, for Their 1,000 Hours of Service
Mayor Ury presented certificates of appreciation to Lela Grossack and Rose Troxel for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center; and Patricia Weeks for volunteer hours with the Mission Viejo Library. Volunteers Debbie Morton, Whalen Malcom, Judi Zimmerman and Michael Smith were unable to attend the meeting.
P3.
Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners
Mayor Ury and Michelle Clark, Waste Management, presented Scott and Vickie Wade with the recycling award.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Desi J. Kiss, M.V.: stated that some of his campaign signs have been stolen and he would like to know what the Sheriff’s department is doing about it. He also questioned whether Mission Viejo is the safest City if California and he asked why his candidate handbook contains misleading information about the City’s top employers.Michael Valdez, M.V.: expressed disappointment with new, illuminated signage at various locations throughout the City and asked why campaign signs are removed by City employees.Joe Tully, M.V.: thanked the City Council Members for the time they give and he outlined a recent public meeting regarding the San Onofre Nuclear Generating station. Mr. Tulley asked the City Council to request that the NRC conduct an injunctive evidentiary hearing. Dan Avery, M.V.: reminded residents that the Council voted 5-0 to not pursue electronic billboards. He also stated that two of the City Council candidates have had an FPPC complaint filed against them and he referred residents to the Mission Viejo Patch for more information.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: outlined the donations that candidates Frank Ury and Wendy Bucknum have received in their campaigns and stated that Mission Viejo voters should not be bought.
Ed Sachs, M.V.: drew the Council’s attention to a notice he received from CalFire regarding a forthcoming bill of up to $150 that he may have to pay because his home is located in a high fire hazard severity zone area.
Matt Corrigan, M.V.: speaking on behalf of resident Paula Steinhauer, he read from a letter she wrote to the Orange County Register regarding her disagreement with the Register’s endorsement of Frank Ury and Wendy Bucknum for City Council.
Harry Lenczyk, M.V. (via email): congratulated the City Council for voting to use budget savings for infastructure improvements and stated that the funds should not be used for a dog park.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
3.
Check Register dated September 21, 2012 in the amount of $2,513,648.22
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated September 28, 2012 in the amount of $490,294.85
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
City Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2012
Received and filed.
6.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2012
Received and filed.
7.
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2012
Received and filed.
8.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2012
Received and filed.
9.
Closure of Library for ILS Migration December 3 to 5, 2012 and Amendment of Library Holiday Hours for 2013 Calendar Year
(1) Approved closure of library from December 3 to 5, 2012, for migration to new ILS system, and (2) approved request to close library from Monday, December 23 - Friday, December 27, 2013. The Library will remain open on Martin Luther King Day, Monday, January 21, Presidents’ Day, Monday, February 18, and Veterans’ Day, Monday, November 11, 2013.
10.
Fourth Amendment to City of Mission Viejo Technical Services Outsourcing Agreement
Approved the Fourth Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Technical Services Outsourcing Agreement with Baker & Taylor, Inc., and increase the purchase order in an amount not to exceed $35,000, for a total of $135,000 for the total term of the two-year Agreement.
11.
Federal-Aid Safe Route To School Project
Adopted Resolution 12-64 Approving and Authorizing Execution of Program Supplement No. N022 to Administering Agency-State Agreement No. 12-5451 for Federal-Aid Projects between the State Department of Transportation and the City of Mission Viejo.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
2.
City Council Minutes
Council Member Schlicht requested that the item be bifurcated since she and Council Member Kelley were absent from the Special Meeting of the Successor Agency on October 1, 2012.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the Minutes for the October 1, 2012, Special Meeting of the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, as presented.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
ABSTAIN:
Council Member Kelley, and Council Member Schlicht.
(Pursuant to City Council Policy, an abstention will be viewed as support for the majority decision.)
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of October 1, 2012, as presented.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
12.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA Board of Directors however she reported on the recent OCFA open house.
13.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury announced that he was unable to attend the last meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA.
14.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
15.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
16.
Status Report on Kaleidoscope’s Signage Ideas or Concepts
City Manager Wilberg presented the report.
Community Development Director Chuck Wilson outlined the history of the proposed signage and meetings that have occurred on the subject.
The following expressed opposition to large, electronic signage at Kaleidoscope: Gail Reavis, M.V. and Joe Tully, M.V.
The City Council received and filed the report.
City Attorney’s Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
17.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
18.
Safety and Resource Fair Addressing Developmental Disabilities
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve plans to organize and host a Safety and Resource Fair for individuals with developmental disabilities and their families.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Kelley expressed her condolences to Ziggy Wilczynski on the loss of his wife, Nina. She discussed her attendance at this year’s Readers’ Festival and she thanked staff for putting on another wonderful event. Council Member Kelley reminded residents that the Walk Against Drugs will be held on Saturday, October 20, 2012. The keynote speaker is former tennis professional Peanut Louie Harper. The event begins at 8:00 a.m. at Mission Viejo High School and after a walk up La Paz Road, participants can enjoy activities at the 5th Annual Disaster Preparedness Expo and Fair. Council Member Kelley invited residents to attend the screening of Cyberbull y which will be shown in the Council Chamber at 2:00 p.m. on October 21. She also announced that Hometown Halloween will be held on October 27 from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center and lastly, Council Member Kelley noted that she and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon were unable to attend the recent meeting regarding the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station because it was closed to further attendees.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness also expressed his condolences to Ziggy Wilczynski and he recounted stories of time he spent with Ziggy and his wife Nina at their home. Council Member Leckness reminded residents of the 2012 Campout with the Mayor from Saturday, October 20 to Sunday, October 21. Lastly he discussed his attendance at the Readers' Festival, noting that he was most impressed by Marcia Clark's presentation.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht expressed her long-term support for the local business community and she referred residents to www.missionviejobusiness.com which was developed to retain, gain and sustain business in Mission Viejo. Council Member Schlicht stated that she is very sad that Nina Wilczynski passed away and her heart and prayers are with Ziggy. She concluded her comments with a quote from Thomas Paine: "Men who look upon themselves born to reign, and others to obey, soon grow insolent; selected from the rest of mankind their minds are early poisoned by importance; and the world they act in differs so materially from the world at large, that they have but little opportunity of knowing its true interests, and when they succeed to the government are frequently the most ignorant and unfit of any throughout the dominions."
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon offered her condolences to Ziggy Wilczynski on the loss of his wife Nina. She informed her colleagues that she asked staff for a status update on the City’s commercial real estate sign enforcement program and she read from Community Development Director Chuck Wilson’s email which outlined overall progress, conformances and challenges. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon noted that staff will return to the City Council in January with a 6-month status update. She also thanked Mr. Wilson for providing an update on the Kaleidoscope signage proposals and she thanked Building Official Jay Elbettar for his announcements on the new building department programs which will help working families. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her attendance at recent events including reading to Kindergartners at Glen Yermo School, a Walk to School Day with Castille Elementary, an immigration reform presentation at Concordia University, and the Saddleback College Foundation breakfast where the speech and debate team made an impressive presentation. She also discussed her attendance at the Readers’ Festival and she thanked Stephanie Tanton and her staff for another wonderful event. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she and Council Member Kelley were unable to attend the recent SONGS meeting because Edison bussed in over 500 Southern California Edison employees and the room became full. She expressed her dissatisfaction and stated that the meeting was supposed to be for the public, not for Edison employees. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon concluded her comments by thanking various staff members and Sheriff’s Department personnel for helping with the three recent drug awareness presentations. She stated that the reality of the prescription drug problem is painful but Mission Viejo wants to be part of the solution.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury stated that the Readers’ Festival was outstanding and he very much enjoyed all of the activities, authors and the Saddleback College dancers. He also reminded residents of the Walk Against Drugs which will be held on Saturday, October 20. Mayor Ury concluded his comments by expressing his heartfelt condolences to Ziggy Wilczynski on the passing of his wife, Nina.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:47 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Nina Wilczynski, to Monday, November 5, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of November 05, 2012
